candidates.attacker_control: Remote, no credentials: the HTTP Content-Type header (and, on the same code path, the multipart Content-Disposition filename embedded in a parser exception message) of a POST request to any URL handled by the Struts filter. The header may both contain the literal substring 'multipart/form-data' (to satisfy Dispatcher.wrapRequest) and carry an OGNL %{...} expression (commons-fileupload rejects it because it does not start with 'multipart/', producing InvalidContentTypeException whose message embeds the raw header).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: 1) Does the crafted header reach the multipart wrapper? Dispatcher.wrapRequest uses content_type.contains("multipart/form-data") (line 800), not startsWith, so a header that fails commons-fileupload's startsWith("multipart/") check still enters MultiPartRequestWrapper and yields InvalidContentTypeException carrying the raw header. 2) Is the default-message path really taken? struts-messages.properties (lines 34-36) defines only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException under struts.messages.upload.error.*; the InvalidContentTypeException key is absent, so findText falls through to getDefaultMessage with e.getMessage(). 3) Is the fallback message OGNL-evaluated? LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage line 662-663 calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack); TextParseUtil line 165-167 delegates to the injected TextParser (bound to OgnlTextParser in XWorkConfigurationProvider line 158) whose evaluate() calls stack.findValue() on each %{...} segment. 4) Is a ValueStack available that early? StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter calls createActionContext (which builds the OgnlValueStack and sets the thread-local ActionContext) before wrapRequest, and Dispatcher.createContextMap populates request/parameters/session. 5) No runtime testing was performed; reachability is inferred from source only. 6) The known upstream advisory/fix for this exact pattern (S2-045, CVE-2017-5638) postdates this 2.3.16.2 snapshot, so the snapshot is expected to still contain it; I could not confirm that VUL4J-29's ground-truth CVE maps to this pattern.
candidates.impact: Server-side OGNL evaluation of attacker-supplied input: arbitrary Java API access through the Struts value stack, enabling remote code execution / command execution in the web-application process (the exact impact class of S2-045/CVE-2017-5638 and S2-046), plus a reflected-content/error-message vector. No authentication, default multipart configuration, and request processing occurs during the prepare phase before action execution.
candidates.prerequisites: Application exposes at least one Struts2 URL (default struts.multipart.parser=jakarta is configured in default.properties); struts.devMode is not required; struts.serve.static and other settings are irrelevant. The ActionContext/ValueStack must be initialized before request wrapping - verified: StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter calls prepare.createActionContext() (which creates the OgnlValueStack) before prepare.wrapRequest() -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest(). A commons-fileupload version whose InvalidContentTypeException message embeds the raw Content-Type is on the classpath (commons-fileupload 1.3.1 is declared in pom.xml).
candidates.root_cause: Multipart requests are detected with a loose substring check and the parser's exception message - which contains the raw, attacker-controlled Content-Type header - is passed as the i18n defaultMessage to LocalizedTextUtil.findText(). When the message key is missing from the bundles (struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException is not defined; only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException are), LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() runs TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack), and the injected OgnlTextParser evaluates each %{...} segment as OGNL against the action ValueStack. The attacker therefore controls an OGNL expression evaluated server-side before the action is even invoked.
candidates.title: Remote OGNL injection / RCE via attacker-controlled multipart Content-Type in Struts' Jakarta multipart error handling
candidates.trace: StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter.doFilter (line 89 createActionContext -> line 91 wrapRequest) -> PrepareOperations.wrapRequest -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest (line 800: content_type.contains("multipart/form-data") is true for a crafted header such as an OGNL expression that also contains that literal) -> new MultiPartRequestWrapper(...) -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse() catch(Exception) -> buildErrorMessage(e, new Object[]{}) (line 118-124) -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText(this.getClass(), "struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException", defaultLocale, e.getMessage(), args). The key is absent from struts-messages*.properties, so getDefaultMessage() (line 648-671) takes the defaultMessage branch and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) at line 663; TextParseUtil obtains the injected TextParser (OgnlTextParser, XWorkConfigurationProvider line 158) and OgnlTextParser.evaluate() hands each %{...} body to TextParseUtil's ParsedValueEvaluator, which calls stack.findValue(...) - i.e. the attacker's OGNL expression is evaluated on the server. The same pattern exists in MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage (line 99-105). Secondary: the resulting error strings are added to action errors by FileUploadInterceptor (line 265-271).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. I did not execute the project, the tests, or any payload; the exploitation step (the exact OGNL expression and gadget/API availability, e.g. #context ObjectFactory access and Runtime/ProcessBuilder availability on the target JDK) was not verified. Commons-fileupload 1.3.1's exact exception text and the servlet container's treatment of an unusual Content-Type header were inferred from source/dependency versions, not executed. I also could not confirm from the source tree which CVE the VUL4J-29 case tracks; the version string 2.3.16.2 suggests a 2014-era fix, whereas the known fix for this pattern is 2.3.32 (2017), which is a discrepancy I could not resolve with the available tools.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-917 Expression Language Injection (leading to CWE-94 Code Injection / RCE); matches the S2-045 (CVE-2017-5638) / S2-046 vulnerability class

coverage_summary: get_source_scope reports 3,826 root files / 3,825 model-visible (one excluded by sensitive-name/path filter; no symlinks; binary-like files skipped). get_relation_scope reports a partial index over 3,825 files (2,016 Java files, 24,800 symbols, 53,040 edges, 847 omitted files, 25 parse errors, 49,869 unresolved calls) with syntax/containment/name-based call and inheritance candidates only - no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or reachability, so every relation was treated as a navigation hint and verified in source text. I inspected the core and xwork-core security surfaces (ParametersInterceptor, ExcludedPatterns, SecurityMemberAccess, CookieInterceptor, multipart/JakartaMultiPartRequest, Dispatcher/wrapRequest, LocalizedTextUtil/TextParseUtil/OgnlTextParser, DefaultActionMapper, I18nInterceptor, DebuggingInterceptor, TokenHelper, DefaultStaticContentLoader, results/tag components, JSON/REST/portlet plugin handlers) plus apps/archetypes for security tests and fixes; the candidate chain was traced and re-verified against source lines. The visible cache contains only Java/XML/properties/txt/js/css/html-type files - no .jsp/.ftl/.vm template bodies are present, so template/tag XSS analysis is limited to Java-side escaping logic.
limitations: No code was executed: no build, unit tests, or exploit payloads; all findings are static and reachability is inferred from source.
The P1 relation index is partial and syntactic (no data/control flow, semantic resolution, Spring profile/DI verification, or runtime enforcement); labels/edges are navigation hints only.
No .jsp/.ftl/.vm templates are visible in the source cache, so FreeMarker/JSP/Velocity output-escaping (a major Struts XSS surface) could not be reviewed.

No git metadata, commit history, changelog, or CVE metadata is available, so I could not confirm which CVE/fix commit VUL4J-29 maps to, nor diff against the fixed revision; the 2.3.16.2 version string conflicts with the 2017 upstream fix for the selected candidate.
Commons-fileupload 1.3.1's exact exception strings and servlet-container header handling were not executed; the injection chain was validated only through the Struts-side code paths.
Excluded/sensitive files (1) and OGNL/index-omitted files were not inspected.

rejected_leads.lead: CookieInterceptor (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/interceptor/CookieInterceptor.java lines 171-337): isAcceptableName() combines a permissive name charset (allows whitespace and single quotes) with ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN matched via Matcher.matches(), so a cookie name such as "x[ 'class' ]..." would not match the excluded pattern while still being accepted, and the name is then compiled and used by stack.setValue(cookieName, cookieValue).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible OGNL/property-path injection when cookiesName="*", but exploitability depends on OGNL tokenization and on the target object graph, which I could not verify without executing; I also found no evidence in the tree that a follow-up fix for this reachable bypass was ever released, so it does not meet the evidence threshold for a candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: TokenHelper.generateGUID() (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/util/TokenHelper.java lines 54, 226-228) uses java.util.Random for CSRF/session tokens (CWE-330).
rejected_leads.reason: Real weakness but low impact relative to the candidate (tokens are stored server-side in the session), and no in-repository fix or CVE association is visible; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: REST plugin XStreamHandler (plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java lines 43-50) deserializes request XML with a plain new XStream() and no type/permission restrictions (S2-052 / CVE-2017-9805 class).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires the REST plugin with application/xml content type (non-default plugin, application-specific setup) and XStream 1.4.2 gadget availability; the known fix is a 2017 release, so it does not fit the 2.3.16.2-era snapshot as the dataset's fix commit; kept as unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: JSON plugin JSONP callback injection: JSONResult.addCallbackIfApplicable / JSONInterceptor.addCallbackIfApplicable concatenate the request callback parameter into JavaScript without validation (plugins/json/.../JSONResult.java lines 246-252).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires enableJSONP/callbackParameter configuration; output is served as application/javascript so the practical impact is limited (content-type/sniffing dependent), and I could not verify any upstream fix for the 2014 window; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: DebuggingInterceptor COMMAND_MODE evaluates the request 'expression' parameter as OGNL (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/interceptor/debugging/DebuggingInterceptor.java lines 189-210).
rejected_leads.reason: Gated on struts.devMode=true/devMode override and on the interceptor being configured, so it is a configuration-dependent debug feature rather than a default-secure-code finding; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: XWorkBasicConverter.doConvertToClass loads arbitrary classes from request parameter values for Class-typed properties (xwork-core/.../XWorkBasicConverter.java lines 160-170).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a Class-typed action property and only performs class loading (no instantiation/evaluation shown); impact and reachability unclear; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Static-content directory traversal (DefaultStaticContentLoader, StaticContentLoaderTest) and showcase FileDownloadAction WEB-INF sanitizer with their tests are already present in this snapshot, and the DefaultUrlHelper '<script'-only escaping plus URL-parameter encoding tests are also present.
rejected_leads.reason: These are the patched (fixed) states, not exploitable as-is in the reviewed snapshot (regression tests included); they were useful chronology markers but are not candidates.

summary: Apache Struts 2 (2.3.16.2 snapshot). The strongest source-evidenced candidate is a remote, unauthenticated OGNL expression injection in the Jakarta multipart request handling: an attacker-controlled Content-Type header is embedded in a commons-fileupload parser exception whose message is used as an i18n fallback/default message, and the fallback path runs the message through TextParseUtil.translateVariables / OgnlTextParser, which evaluates it as OGNL against the request ValueStack (the S2-045 / CVE-2017-5638 pattern, also reachable via the Content-Disposition filename, S2-046). Default configuration reaches it: struts.multipart.parser=jakarta and the default interceptor stack fileUpload; Dispatcher.wrapRequest only requires the header to *contain* "multipart/form-data" (it may start with an OGNL expression), and the resulting InvalidContentTypeException has no message key in struts-messages.properties, so the attacker string is used verbatim as the default message. Other leads (CookieInterceptor name-pattern bypass, predictable token Random, REST XStreamHandler, JSONP callback injection, devMode-gated DebuggingInterceptor console) are weaker and listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
